text.p: The central bank provided 31.8 trillion lira of funds to the interbank market after starting Thursday trade with "tomorrow next value" on its screen-based money market.
The bank set its t/n bid and offer rates at 59-76 percent on Thursday and also lowered its overnight offer rate to 78 percent from Wednesday's 80.
The bank also raised its overnight bid rate to 57 percent from 55, narrowing the margin between its bid and offer rates to 57-78 from a previous 55-80 percent.

The central bank lent 16.2 trillion lira overnight at 78 percent in late trade, up from the 14.1 trillion lira it injected at 80 percent on Wednesday. It also injected 15.6 trillion lira at 76 percent via t/n deals.
Overnight money traded between 76.5 and 78 percent earlier in the day. The money market had opened with a 12.6 trillion lira surplus.
The lira closed weaker at 103,650 against the dollar versus Wednesday's 103,480.

Bankers said the banks' dollar demand firmed on lower overnight money rates. The lira fell sharply to a low of 103,800 to the dollar in the morning, but it firmed to 103,650 on the central bank's minor intervention in the afternoon.

The central bank set its dollar rate for banks' compulsory foreign currency transfers at 103,350 lira at the opening, up from Wednesday's 103,300 lira close, and further raised it to 103,400 at close.
Yields on t-bills and bonds plunged by up to four points on lower overnight money rates.

The average yield on the most heavily traded Sept 3, 1997 paper fell to 114.08 from Wednesday's 117.98 percent. The second most active October 30, 1997 paper yielded 114.15, down from Wednesday's 117.59 percent average.
